subtitle: Lesson 21 · Core ITIL 4 Practices: Request, Knowledge & Service Level

code:
Purpose: set clear, business-based targets for
service levels, and ensure delivery is properly
assessed, monitored, and managed against them.

A target nobody tracks is decoration,
not management.
caption: Setting the target is half the job; watching it is the other half.

steps.label: SLA
steps.sub: the business-facing promise between provider and customer

steps.label: OLA
steps.sub: internal agreement between teams who must cooperate to hit the SLA

steps.label: Underpinning contract
steps.sub: external contract with a supplier the SLA depends on

code:
Component metric: "server uptime: 99.9%"
-- can be true while the business still suffers.

Output-based target: "orders placed and
confirmed within 5 seconds, 99% of the time"
-- what the business actually experiences.
caption: Component metrics diagnose; output-based targets get reported.

code:
Signing the SLA is the start, not the finish.

Ongoing work:
- continuous performance monitoring
- regular service review meetings
- renegotiation when targets prove unrealistic
caption: A pattern of SLA breaches is exactly what a review should surface.
